text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: Critical - API Gateway elevated 5xx (502/504) spike in us-east-1. alert_id=pdu-5179991234, severity=critical :rotating_light:

pagerduty: @morgan @tariq @lee — oncall escalation sent. runbook: ingress-5xx-spike.

morgan: @here seeing a big jump in 502/504s from the edge -> gateway layer. dashboards show 5xx rate from 0.5% to ~9% in last 4m. p95 latency +2.3s.

tariq: I'm oncall, joining. starting quick triage. which region?

morgan: us-east-1 primarily (us-east-1a/b). small bump in eu-west but negligible.

lee: jumping in now. any pattern in upstreams?

morgan: traces point to upstream pool A (backend-pool-a) returning connection failures and some timeouts. I see Nginx errors like:

```
[error] 12345#0: *9876 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.0.0.5, server: api, request: "POST /v1/generate", upstream: "http://10.2.3.4:8080/v1/generate", host: "api.redwood.ai"
```

morgan: curl against gateway returns 502: `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health` -> HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway

tariq: can someone paste `kubectl top` for backend pods? suspect CPU throttling or OOMs.

lee: running now: `kubectl -n prod top pods -l app=backend-pool-a` -> one pod at 98% CPU, others 72-80%. No OOMs logged.

morgan: logs show increasing backlog: `accept queue full` and intermittent `connect() to 10.2.3.4:8080 failed (111: Connection refused)`. Looks like ephemerally overwhelmed upstreams.

jess: initial customer impact: from metrics, ~12% of total requests in us-east are returning 5xx. Support dashboards show ~37 clients with >1% error. Two larger customers (acme-inc, beta-co) reporting elevated errors. We should prepare comms.

support-bot: Notified #support-inbox and created ticket TCK-1129 (severity=high). Draft message suggested: "We're investigating increased errors in us-east, degraded performance for some API routes. We'll update in 15 minutes."

tariq: mitigation plan: 1) shift traffic from backend-pool-a to pool-b (fallback) 2) increase replicas for pool-a 3) enable ephemeral circuit breaker in gateway to reduce fanout. Which order is safest?

lee: Recommend enabling circuit breaker first to reduce failed connections and prevent cascading resource exhaustion. Then shift a fraction of traffic to pool-b (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%). Finally scale pool-a if needed.

morgan: rolling circuit breaker now: applying envoy config change. command: `kubectl apply -f /ops/envoy/circuit-breaker-us-east.yaml`

incident-bot: Deploy started by morgan - change id deploy-517999-1.

morgan: envoy change applied. observed immediate drop in connection attempts to backend-pool-a from edge -> pool-a by ~60%. 5xx rate decreased from ~9% to ~4.2% in 2m.

tariq: good. start traffic shift to pool-b at 10%: updating trafficsplit. `kubectl apply -f /ops/trafficshift/poolb-10pc.yaml`

morgan: pool-b 10% applied. monitoring.

lee: pool-b healthy. backend pool-b pods at ~45-60% CPU. No errors seen.

morgan: after 5m at 10%: 5xx now 2.1% and trending down. p95 latency improving.

jess: preparing customer update: ETA for stabilization ~ 20-30 minutes if trends continue. @support-bot queue the message; include suggestion to retry with exponential backoff.

support-bot: Draft queued to #support-inbox. Will post after approval.

tariq: scaling pool-a replicas by +3 as precaution: `kubectl scale deployment backend-pool-a --replicas=8 -n prod`

morgan: scale acknowledged. new pods spinning up, readiness checks passing.

lee: We should also audit any recent deploys to pool-a. Rollouts?

morgan: No deploys in last 2 hours to pool-a. Most recent was an infra config change 6h ago.

tariq: OK. current status: 5xx at 0.9% and declining, p95 latency down 1.1s. Customer errors substantially reduced. Still monitoring for any resurgence.

jess: Support comms approved, posting now. Linking to status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/5179991234

support-bot: Posted customer message to #support-inbox and sent to affected customers list.

morgan: incident summary for handoff: root cause likely transient overload of backend-pool-a (connection queue saturation). Mitigations: enabled circuit breaker at ingress, shifted traffic to pool-b, scaled pool-a. impact: max ~12% of us-east requests, top customers impacted: acme-inc, beta-co.

tariq: handing off to lee for next-oncall starting at 03:15Z. I'll remain available for escalations.

lee: taking the handoff. I'll keep monitoring for 30m and then close. Great coordination. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident pdu-5179991234 status=stabilized. Actions logged: clf-517999-ops. Please file follow-up RCA if necessary.

morgan: filing quick postmortem link: https://workspace.redwood.ai/pm/notes/517999-postmortem

lee: closing thread for now, will re-open if we see regression.
